# `aitbc config get`

Print the stored value of one config key. Without a key, shows the current configuration (alias for show). With a key, prints its stored value; exits nonzero when the key is absent, and refuses sensitive key names outright.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc config get [OPTIONS] [KEY]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | text | no | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--global` | flag | `false` | no | Read the global config file |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc config get
```
